articles.title: Chelsea manager Alonso insists Cole Palmer is committed to playing for England
articles.summary: Palmer pulled out of England squad due to injury. Attacker available for Chelsea’s game with Bournemouth. Xabi Alonso has said Cole Palmer is committed to playing for England and revealed Chelsea’s No 10 missed this international break with a problem related to the groin injury that kept him out…
body: Thomas Tuchel did not hide his disappointment with Palmer, who is fit to face Bournemouth on Saturday, after the attacker made himself unavailable for the start of his country’s Nations League campaign last month. Tuchel said the 24-year-old “misses too many opportunities” to play for England and questioned whether Palmer wanted to be part of the squad.

Palmer has won five caps since scoring against Spain in the Euro 2024 final but his latest withdrawal was for genuine reasons. Palmer struggled with persistent groin pain last season, which led to him missing out on a place in Tuchel’s World Cup squad, and felt minor irritation before Chelsea’s defeat by Brentford last month. It still needs careful management, and Alonso is adamant Chelsea’s talisman is intent on playing for England.

“The most important thing for Cole is to be fully fit, that he enjoys his game, that he is feeling OK,” Chelsea’s manager said. “Whenever he is not, like in the Brentford game, we could see that he was struggling. He’s committed but he needs to be fully fit to play. We need him – the club and the national team.”

articles.title: West Ham’s penalty pain costs them top spot in Championship after QPR draw
articles.summary: The QPR goalkeeper Pierce Charles made a stunning double save from a Jarrod Bowen penalty in stoppage time to secure a 1-1 draw at West Ham. The 21-year-old, who kept four clean sheets and saved a penalty for Northern Ireland over the international break, pulled off more heroics to deny the Hammers…
body: Bowen had already equalised for West Ham, cancelling out a hugely controversial first-half penalty from Nicolas Madsen. But the Hammers captain saw his spot-kick saved and Charles then somehow pushed the rebound from Arne Engels on to the crossbar.

West Ham were earlier on the wrong end of a dreadful penalty decision after Tomas Soucek was penalised for fouling Paul Smyth. Replays showed the challenge was well outside the area and that the Hammers midfielder got the ball. A VAR review would have definitely overturned referee Ruebyn Ricardo’s decision but with no technology in the Championship it stood, to the dismay of the majority inside the London Stadium.
The West Ham assistant coach Rui Pedro Silva was booked for his complaints, as was Engels for stamping on the penalty spot, but Madsen kept his cool and calmly rolled the ball into the bottom corner.

Rangers almost doubled their lead from a West Ham corner, mounting a swift counterattack which left recalled striker Rayan Kolli with a shooting opportunity 15 yards out, but Mads Hermansen made a fine save.

articles.title: Man City whistleblower to remain in witness protection
articles.summary: The computer hacker who released documents which helped trigger the Premier League investigation into Manchester City will remain under witness protection after authorities in Portugal suspend the decision to end it.
body: The Portuguese computer hacker who released documents which helped trigger the Premier League investigation into Manchester City will remain in witness protection after authorities in the country suspended the decision to end it.
Football Leaks founder Rui Pinto had been scheduled to leave the protection programme on Saturday, a ruling he previously said had put him in a "life-threatening situation".
Pinto, 37, disclosed a tranche of confidential football documents, including emails and financial records relating to the English Premier League side.
In 2018, he shared documents with German magazine Der Spiegel, which used them for investigations into City's finances and alleged breaches of financial fair play rules.

articles.title: The Premier League is back: welcome to the new era of post-verdict unreality | Barney Ronay
articles.summary: As the top flight returns, armed with the knowledge its serial champions have been the authors of a 10-year sham supremacy, the first question is simple: how is it going to feel? The internet: an apology. It turns out you were right. It was actually a simulation all along.
body: Welcome to the weirdest weekend of them all. We are now post-judgment, post-statement, postlapsarian. As the Premier League prepares to snap back into what must be described, out of habit, as reality, armed with the knowledge its serial champions have been the authors of a 10-year sham supremacy, the first question is fairly simple. How is it going to feel?

There is no precedent for this. Even the state of total confusion feels brittle given City maintain their complete state of innocence and deny all charges. We await the release of Irrefutable Body of Evidence, the great lost Madonna erotic thriller sequel, presumably recast around a steamy three-year regulatory tribunal scenario.

City’s appeal defence appears to be based around the government giving them money. This may or may not be related to how you control what the high court considers admissible. But it is also implied confirmation that the club is the propaganda tool of an overseas state, that Kyle Walker, for example, has basically been a civil servant all these years. Maybe the United Arab Emirates should have six stars on the national team jersey, one for each title. They even look like asterisks.

articles.title: Lionesses take control of World Cup playoff tie but unfancied Greece still in fight
articles.summary: World Cup qualifying playoff: Greece 1-3 England. Stanway, Le Tissier and Russo on target. Sarina Wiegman said she wanted to see a bit more from her side after their fairly underwhelming performance against a hugely unfancied Greek side, despite securing a valuable first-leg victory in their…
body: Georgia Stanway’s neat finish, Maya Le Tissier’s first England goal and Alessia Russo’s low strike were enough to give England control but a Kallisti Brouksair goal for Greece means that the tie is not definitively over, going into Tuesday’s second leg, and Wiegman acknowledged that England had been “a bit sloppy” at times.

“I think we made it a bit harder [for ourselves],” Wiegman said, while also giving credit to Greece for being “very well-prepared, very well-organised and very disciplined”, before adding: “Of course, I’m happy with the 3-1. I’m not happy with the 1.
“We were – in moments – really good on the ball, and we were, in moments, not so good on the ball and we could have made better decisions, too.
“We want to play really well. Of course, we go out to win, but we want to show more than winning, we want to play really well too.”

articles.title: NI World Cup hopes gone from 'improbable to impossible'
articles.summary: Michael McArdle admits Northern Ireland's chances of beating Portugal in a Women's World Cup play-off have "gone from improbable to impossible" after a 4-0 first leg defeat.
body: Underdogs heading into the first-leg tie, the hosts were well beaten and face a mammoth task to overturn the deficit in Tuesday's return in Portimao.
McArdle, who took over as Northern Ireland manager in March, felt there were positives in the defeat, but said the scoreline was "sore" and "it hurts".
"It feels a bit harder on us than the actual game produced," added the Scot.
"We're hurting in that aspect. There are lots of positives there, which we'll take and we'll move forward for the longer process.

articles.title: 'Bored' White credits Hearn for Fury-Joshua being in UK
articles.summary: Dana White gives credit to Eddie Hearn, but says he is "bored" of the ongoing feud between him and his rival promoter.
body: Dana White has credited Eddie Hearn for making sure the long-awaited fight between Tyson Fury and Antony Joshua will be held in the UK but insisted he was "bored" of their ongoing feud.

The heavyweight bout will take place at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff - despite efforts to host it New York's Madison Square Garden - on a bill that starts on 11 December, though they are not expected to fight until the early hours of 12 December.
White and Saudi Arabian organisers wanted the bout in the United States, but Joshua and his promoter Hearn refused to budge on their contractual right to have it in the UK.

"You've got to give credit to Eddie for really grinding that and making sure that it happened in the UK," UFC president and Zuffa Boxing chief White told Steve Bunce on the 5 Live Boxing with Bunce podcast.

articles.title: 'You will see me back' - Smith vows 2027 return after Swiss Darts Trophy win
articles.summary: Former world champion Michael Smith says he plans on "playing 100 per cent of the tournaments" in 2027 after an opening win at the Swiss Darts Trophy.
body: 'Bully Boy' Smith fought back from 3-1 down to beat Rob Owen, hitting 50 per cent of his doubles in just his fourth European Tour event of the season.
"I've missed this. I want to apologise and also make a promise in 2027 I will be playing 100 per cent of the tournaments. You will see me back," said the 2023 world champion.
Smith is chasing down the final spots in the European Championship race and the St Helens thrower beat Owen 6-4 to set up a meeting with Jermaine Wattimena for a place in Sunday's action.

Rob Cross was Friday's standout performer for the second event in a row, averaging 105.95 in his 6-3 success against Mario Vandenbogaerde and will take on Luke Woodhouse on the back of his brilliant opening round performance at the World Grand Prix.
